summary: Kaniksu National Forest L-4 lookout: 1920s tent camp, 1934 40-ft pole tower replaced it, destroyed 1966; no source describes the site today.

events.note: 40-ft pole tower with L-4 cab replaced the 1920s platform and tent camp
Kamstra and Kemnow both give 1966. Sources give no cause.

evidence.supports: 1920s camp with tent and 20-ft platform tower
evidence.quote: Developed in the 1920's with a 20' platform tower and a tent,

evidence.supports: 40-ft L-4 tower replaced the earlier structure in 1934
Location three miles northwest of Upper Priest Lake
evidence.quote: 3 miles northwest of Upper Priest Lake

evidence.supports: Patrol tower 3/4 mile northeast in the 1934 entry

corrections.why: 6.1 m is 20 ft, the 1920s platform. The 1934 L-4 tower was 40 ft (12.2 m), which the story and facts use.

sources.title: Gold Peak - Forest Lookouts
sources.publisher: Ron Kemnow, Forest Lookouts western US

notes_for_editor: Height correction: the record's 6.1 m is the 20-ft 1920s platform, not the 1934 L-4 tower (40 ft = 12.2 m). The 1920s camp is decade-only, so it is left out of events. Kemnow's 1934 entry also lists a 40-ft platform patrol tower 3/4 mile NE, which is not in the record. No staffing sources. No source describes the site today or gives access. Elevation 4534 ft is in the story but has no facts key.
